Subject: RFI: Cross-border processing & KMS residency — VeloxCare

Hi Avery,

Thanks for the quick intro call yesterday. As part of our procurement review we need a concise set of clarifications around cross-border processing and key management for inference traffic. Our security team asked for the following items so we can close the privacy chapter: 

1) Confirmation of where customer request payloads and inference logs may be processed (US/EU/APAC). If routing varies by model/region, please provide the routing logic and fallback behavior.
2) Details on key management options and whether customer-managed keys (CMKs) can be used with HSM-backed keys located in our chosen region.
3) DPA annex: can you support a clause that requires no cross-border export of personal data outside specified jurisdictions for hosted workloads (short of Dedicated or Private)?
4) Temporary cache/KV-residency: how long is KV/prefix cache retained and where is cached state stored?
5) Subprocessor list and evidence (SOC2 snapshot or equivalent) and an export controls statement for models hosted by Redwood.

If you can send a short written response and any supporting artifacts (matrix, DPA annex draft, SOC2 snapshot) by next Wednesday 08/09 we'd appreciate it. We may follow with a short 30-minute technical call.

Best,

From: Avery Johnson <avery.johnson@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: RFI: Cross-border processing & KMS residency — VeloxCare

Hi Priya — thanks for the list. Apologies for the slightly longer turnaround; attached is a concise package that addresses each point. Key highlights below, and the attached artifacts are referenced inline.

1) Processing & routing (attachment: redwood-region-routing-matrix.csv) - Hosted API: requests are routed by policy (region preference, model compatibility, latency). By default, inference requests are routed to the nearest available region; for VeloxCare we can pin routing to US-only by SLA or via Dedicated/Private deployment. Fallback behavior: when capacity in the pinned region is exhausted, requests will failover to a compatible model in the same legal region when available; cross-border failover is disabled when "region lock" is requested in the DPA annex. See the routing matrix for typical model-region mappings.

2) Key Management (attachment: kms-residency-notes.txt) - Hosted customers can use Redwood-managed keys or Customer-Managed Keys (CMK) integrated with external KMS via standard KMIP or cloud KMS APIs. For CMKs, we support HSM-backed keys and can configure key residency in supported cloud regions (AWS KMS, Azure Key Vault, GCP KMS). Note: outbound wrapped key operations for inference may require a short-lived envelope key exchange; Redwood does not export unwrapped customer private keys. For the strictest residency guarantees we recommend Dedicated or Private deployments where the entire inference stack (and HSM) is provisioned inside your VPC/region.

3) DPA Annex language (attachment: DPA-Annex-VeloxCare.pdf) - We've drafted an addendum that provides:
  - explicit region-locking option for hosted workloads (if selected, Redwood will not route or replicate personal data outside the enumerated jurisdictions),
  - obligations and escalation for emergency cross-border operations (requires written approval),
  - audit rights and a 30-day SLA for notification of subprocessor changes.
If you'd like alternative wording (e.g., absolute prohibition vs operational assurances), we can iterate.

4) KV/Prefix cache residency - KV cache is ephemeral by design and intended for active sessions. Default retention is 72 hours for inferred KV entries; we can reduce TTL to the minimum operational value or disable persistent prefix caching for VeloxCare. Cache shards are colocated with the serving region; the routing matrix indicates cache residency per region.

5) Subprocessors & Evidence (attachment: SOC2-snapshot.pdf) - Attached is a current SOC2 snapshot and a pointer to our subprocessors registry. We also included an export-controls statement in the SOC appendix. For procurement: we can provide a formal attestation and a fuller control mapping under an NDA if required.

Next steps
- If VeloxCare signs the attached DPA addendum, we will lock routing and KMS residency according to the annex within 5 business days for hosted customers (or immediately upon Dedicated/Private provisioning).
- We propose a 30-minute technical call next week to walk the VeloxCare security team through the routing matrix and KMS flow. Please propose two 30-minute slots.

Attachments included: redwood-region-routing-matrix.csv; DPA-Annex-VeloxCare.pdf; kms-residency-notes.txt; SOC2-snapshot.pdf
